title: "Lab 14: Many Models Without Losing The Evidence"
execute:
  enabled: false
---

## Goal

Apply one checked model contract across five monthly subsets while retaining
every fit, result, uncertainty interval, diagnostic, and source identifier.

## Setup

Create:

```text
week14/
  week14-many-models.R
  week14-grouped-sensitivity.R
```

Download:

- [week14-many-models.R](../code/r/week14-many-models.R)
- [week14-grouped-sensitivity.R](../code/r/week14-grouped-sensitivity.R)

The scripts use R's built-in `airquality` data.

## Part A: State What Stays Fixed

Write the shared model contract: observation, response, predictors, formula,
units, complete-case rule, minimum group size, summary schema, diagnostic
thresholds, and sensitivity rule.

## Part B: Check The Grouped Inputs

Create the ordered month factor, split the data, and produce an input audit with
group name, row count, and predictor ranges.

Reconcile the group names, order, and total rows before fitting.

## Part C: Test One Fit

Run `fit_one_month` on May. Confirm its input checks, `lm` object, formula,
coefficient names, interval bounds, training RMSE, and R-squared.

Trigger one expected failure, then restore the valid input.

## Part D: Retain Every Model

Apply the function to all five months. Name the result list and combine the
one-row summaries. Check that no group disappeared and every model uses the
same formula text.

## Part E: Visualize Coefficients Honestly

Plot temperature coefficients with 95% intervals. Annotate or accompany the
plot with monthly sample sizes. Write two observations that respect uncertainty
and do not name a winner.

## Part F: Repeat Diagnostics

Run `week14-grouped-sensitivity.R`. Check one diagnostic record per month and
trace every selected sensitivity row back to its original observation ID.

Inspect the three groups whose temperature coefficients change by more than
40%.

## Part G: Explain The Training-Error Trap

All sensitivity training RMSE values fall after removing the selected row.
Explain why selection and changed row sets make this an unfair basis for a
predictive improvement claim.

## Part H: Project 2 Transfer

Map the grouped workflow habits to Project 2: frozen formula, result schema,
source identifiers, sensitivity record, and validation evidence. Identify
which classroom monthly results are not required by the project.

## Deliverable

Submit:

- fixed contract and grouped-input audit;
- named list of five complete model results;
- aligned coefficient and metric table;
- coefficient plot with intervals and sample sizes;
- grouped diagnostic and sensitivity table;
- two supported cross-group observations and one rejected ranking claim;
- Project 2 transfer notes.

## AI Use

If an LLM automates or ranks the models, record the full group list, expected
result schema, omitted evidence, generated ranking rule, and repaired
interpretation.
